summary: GRAVEYARD causal pass covered all 12 active-batch names and preserved explicit thesis breakers around concentration, substitution, export/geopolitical exposure, bottleneck migration and AI-capex common-mode risk. None is ready for Chief promotion.

evidence: Launch/satellite systems connect space access to communications and national-security infrastructure
unresolvedGaps: Neutron qualification economics/schedule and backlog sensitivity
falsifiersUnknowns: reusable-launch competition or Neutron delay breaks scale path

evidence: Connectivity relieves bandwidth/power bottlenecks; concentrated customers expose value-capture fragility
unresolvedGaps: customer insourcing and successor optical architecture
contradictions: Bottleneck importance can rise while merchant value capture falls

evidence: PCIe/CXL addresses composability and memory-bandwidth constraints
unresolvedGaps: end-customer mapping and durable CXL monetization
falsifiersUnknowns: CXL stalls or integration moves into platform silicon

evidence: Accelerated compute remains central training/inference bottleneck
unresolvedGaps: custom-accelerator substitution, export-control sensitivity, indirect concentration
contradictions: Compute scarcity supports pricing while custom silicon can migrate value away from merchant GPU

evidence: Second-source accelerator/CPU capacity improves compute-stack resilience
Custom AI silicon/networking benefits from migration toward workload-specific compute
contradictions: Custom silicon substitutes for GPU but is itself concentrated around few builders

evidence: Leading-edge foundry remains a cross-vendor physical bottleneck
unresolvedGaps: geographic diversification economics and customer concentration
contradictions: Dominant bottleneck paired with Taiwan geopolitical single-region risk
falsifiersUnknowns: geopolitical interruption or viable process alternative

evidence: EUV/High-NA remains upstream of leading-edge compute and memory
unresolvedGaps: critical supplier single points and export-control demand migration
contradictions: Near-monopoly bottleneck is politically exposed and supplier-dependent

evidence: CPU architecture/IP spans edge/mobile/cloud while monetization/control remains concentrated
contradictions: Architecture ubiquity does not equal diversified revenue capture

evidence: HBM/memory bandwidth is a successor bottleneck as accelerator compute scales
unresolvedGaps: HBM supply-demand duration and capex response
contradictions: Structural need coexists with commodity-cycle mean reversion
falsifiersUnknowns: capacity additions outrun AI memory demand

evidence: Ethernet scale-out networking grows in importance with cluster size
unresolvedGaps: white-box/custom fabric substitution and customer dependence
contradictions: Open Ethernet expands TAM while enabling alternatives
falsifiersUnknowns: hyperscaler custom networking captures switching value

evidence: Power delivery/thermal management are physical successor bottlenecks after compute procurement
unresolvedGaps: backlog conversion quality and customer concentration
contradictions: Structural demand can remain strong while project timing weakens realized economics
falsifiersUnknowns: AI capex slowdown or cooling/power commoditization

contradictions: Cross-stack diversification does not equal demand-regime diversification: the batch remains heavily correlated to AI/data-center capex.
Bottlenecks can migrate GPU -> HBM/networking -> power/cooling -> grid/energy; today's chokepoint is not permanent.
unknowns: rate at which grid constraints cap compute deployment
peerRequests: Discovery: keep searching substitute architectures; red team: stress synchronized hyperscaler capex slowdown.
blockingIssues: No active-batch company is structural-causal ready_for_chief this cycle.
